question: explain batch and streaming in simple words

plain.answer: Batch processing involves handling data in large chunks, like a full day's worth of data at once [Ch. 2]. Streaming, on the other hand, processes data continuously and in real-time, as it is produced [Ch. 2]. Batch processing is often used for analytics and machine learning tasks where data is ingested on a predetermined schedule [Ch. 2]. Streaming is more suitable for applications requiring real-time data processing, such as financial trading or online analytics [Ch. 2].

plain3.answer: Batch processing involves handling data in large chunks at predetermined intervals or when a preset size is reached [Ch. 2]. Streaming ingestion provides data to downstream systems continuously and in real-time [Ch. 2]. Batch processing is popular in analytics and machine learning [Ch. 2]. Micro-batching is a way to use batch-oriented frameworks for streaming situations, running every two minutes to every second [Ch. 8]. True streaming systems process one event at a time, though they may still operate in batches [Ch. 8].

question: explain the data mesh in simple words

plain.answer: The data mesh is a way to manage data in a company by breaking it into smaller, more manageable pieces. Instead of having all data stored in one central place, data mesh suggests that each team owns and serves its own data. This approach helps to avoid the problems of large, centralized data platforms. In data mesh, every team is responsible for preparing their data for use by other teams and for their own analytics. [Ch. 3] [Ch. 9]

plain3.answer: The data mesh is a decentralized approach to managing data, reversing the traditional centralized model. [Ch. 3] Each domain team owns and serves its data, preparing it for consumption by other teams. [Ch. 9] This changes how data is served within an organization, with every domain team responsible for both serving and consuming data. [Ch. 9] The data mesh includes four key components: domain-oriented decentralized data ownership, data as a product, self-serve data infrastructure, and federated computational governance. [Ch. 3]

question: explain when an insert-only table is useful in simple words

plain.answer: An insert-only table is useful when you want to maintain a current view of data without deleting old records [Ch. 8]. This approach can be helpful in applications that need to access historical data, such as a banking application that needs to show a customer's address history [Ch. 5]. However, it can be computationally expensive to find the latest record at query time [Ch. 8].

plain3.answer: An insert-only table is useful for maintaining a current view of data [Ch. 8]. It allows new records to be inserted without changing or deleting old records [Ch. 8]. This pattern can be used in applications that need access to history, such as a banking application [Ch. 5]. However, it can be computationally expensive to find the latest record at query time [Ch. 8]. Insert-only tables are often used with regular CRUD application tables in the insert-only ETL pattern [Ch. 5].
